about: Every source of the titration lab's record (docs/research/phase-3/titration.json), each fetched and read on the retrieval date. A source with `file` has its copy in this folder, as downloaded, with the sha256 of that copy; a source with none was read and no copy is kept. `alsoKept` lists a second copy of the same record fetched from another address. Each `supports` row names one stored value by its path in the record, gives in `prints` the figure or label exactly as the source prints it, and says in `where`, in this project's words, where it is. A bottle's `reference` in the record is the name of the classification's source in the kept PubChem copy, a colon and a space, and the entry's name with the space around it removed. README.md in this folder gives the attribution the two Wikipedia copies require.

sources.citation: Tamura, Z.; Abe, S.; Ito, K.; Maeda, M. Spectrophotometric Analysis of the Relationship between Dissociation and Coloration, and of the Structural Formulas of Phenolphthalein in Aqueous Solution. Anal. Sci. 1996, 12 (6), 927-930. https://doi.org/10.2116/analsci.12.927 (read as the publisher's PDF on J-STAGE, linked here; retrieved 2026-10-04).

supports.where: The abstract, and the results on page 929: the first of phenolphthalein's two acid constants, estimated from absorption spectra measured in 0.2 M phosphate buffers at 25 ± 2 °C.

The same two places: the second acid constant. The abstract says that only the form that has lost both protons is coloured, and gives a third constant of 12 for the slow fading in strong base, which the model leaves out.

sources.citation: International Association for the Properties of Water and Steam. IAPWS R11-24, Revised Release on the Ionization Constant of H2O (2024) (retrieved 2026-10-04).

supports.where: Table 3, the first row (liquid water at 0.1 MPa below 100 °C), the column for 25 °C: the release's pK_w. Section 3 says the model takes the ions on the molal standard state.

Table 2, the release's own test value at 300 K and a density of 1.0 g/cm³. The equations (2) to (4), written out with the parameters of Table 1, were checked against it before being worked at 298.15 K and 0.99705 g/cm³, where they give 13.994.

sources.citation: Lemmon, E. W.; Bell, I. H.; Huber, M. L.; McLinden, M. O. Thermophysical Properties of Fluid Systems. In NIST Chemistry WebBook, NIST Standard Reference Database Number 69; Linstrom, P. J., Mallard, W. G., Eds.; National Institute of Standards and Technology: Gaithersburg, MD. https://doi.org/10.18434/T4D303 Isobaric properties for water at 0.1 MPa and 25 °C (retrieved 2026-10-04).

supports.where: The table of isobaric data at 0.1 MPa, its one row (25 °C), the density column in kg/m³. It is the density of liquid water used to work the release's equation and to convert pK_w from the molal to the molar scale.

sources.citation: NIST Chemistry WebBook, NIST Standard Reference Database Number 69; Linstrom, P. J., Mallard, W. G., Eds.; National Institute of Standards and Technology: Gaithersburg, MD. Carbon dioxide, Henry's Law data, compiled by R. Sander (retrieved 2026-10-04).

supports.where: The table of Henry's law data, the column for the constant for solubility in water at 298.15 K, in mol/(kg*bar). Eleven of its seventeen rows print this figure; the others print 0.035 three times and 0.045, 0.032 and 0.031 once each. On the retrieval date no row named its reference.

sources.citation: NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory. Trends in Atmospheric Carbon Dioxide: globally averaged marine surface annual mean data (co2_annmean_gl.txt), file created 2026-09-05 (retrieved 2026-10-04). See https://gml.noaa.gov/ccgg/trends/ for the method.

supports.where: The row for the year 2025, the column of means, beside an uncertainty of 0.05. The file's header gives the unit as a mole fraction in dry air in micromoles per mole (ppm), and says that the last year's figure may still be revised.

sources.citation: Perrin, D. D., Ed. Ionisation Constants of Inorganic Acids and Bases in Aqueous Solution, 2nd ed.; IUPAC Chemical Data Series 29; Pergamon: Oxford, 1982. The book was not read: the two constants were taken from a secondary transcription, Wikipedia's article Carbonic acid, revision 1376246456 of 2026-09-23, linked here, whose infobox cites the book's entry for carbonic acid (retrieved 2026-10-04).

supports.where: The infobox's acidity line, the second of its three figures, the one marked hydrous, with no temperature beside it. The first figure, 3.75, is marked anhydrous and 25 °C and is not the one the model uses. The page's section on bicarbonate and carbonate prints 6.35 again for this constant, and before it 6.77, worked out for 25 °C and a solution with no other ions.

The same line of the infobox, its third figure, with no temperature beside it: the second constant. The page's section on bicarbonate and carbonate prints 9.93 for this constant and, with the 6.35, a difference of 3.49 between the two.

sources.citation: Ricca Chemical Company. Catalogue listing for product number 5600 (R5600000), a phenolphthalein indicator solution of 0.5% (w/v) in 50% (v/v) alcohol, neutralized (retrieved 2026-10-04).

supports.where: The page's title and the product's heading: the strength of the solution, a percentage.
Directly after the percentage sign in the same heading: the basis the listing states, weight per volume.
The same heading, after the strength: the solvent. The listing does not say which alcohol; the heading ends with the word Neutralized.
The table of reference methods lower on the page, in the reagent name of an ASTM method this product serves: the same strength as a mass in a volume, which is 0.5 g in 100 mL.

sources.citation: Fisher Scientific Company. Safety Data Sheet: Hydrochloric Acid Solution, 0.1N (Certified), catalogue number SA54; revision 7 of 18 December 2025 (retrieved 2026-10-04).

supports.where: Section 2, label elements: the signal word.

Section 2, classification: the category for skin corrosion or irritation, and again for serious eye damage or eye irritation. The hazard statements under the signal word say that the solution irritates the skin and causes serious irritation of the eyes.
Section 2, classification: the category for corrosion of metals, with a hazard statement that the solution may corrode them.
Section 3: the weight percent of hydrochloric acid in the solution, the rest being water. The sheet gives no closer figure, so the note's 0.4% is worked out and not read.
Section 4, first aid: the least time to rinse the eyes, and to wash the skin, with plenty of water.
Section 8: the heading of the row that calls for protective glasses or goggles. The row after it calls for gloves and protective clothing.

supports.where: Section 2, label elements. The classification above it says that the product is not considered hazardous under the United States hazard communication standard of 2024.
Section 3: the weight percent of sodium hydroxide in the solution, the rest being water. The note's 0.4% is worked out and not read; it is the top of this range.
Section 4, first aid: the least time to rinse the eyes, and to wash the skin, with plenty of water.
Section 8: the heading of the row that calls for protective glasses or goggles. The row after it calls for gloves and protective clothing.

sources.citation: Ricca Chemical Company. Safety Data Sheet: Phenolphthalein Indicator, 0.5% (w/v) in 50% (v/v) Alcohol, Neutralized, product number 5600; last revised 2026-05-25 (retrieved 2026-10-04).

supports.where: Section 1.1, the product number: the sheet is for the solution of the catalogue listing the indicator's strength is read from.
Section 2.2, label elements: the signal word.
Sections 2.1 and 2.2: flammable liquids, category 3; the liquid and its vapour are flammable.
The same sections: eye irritation, category 2; serious irritation of the eyes.
The same sections: carcinogenicity, category 1B; the solution may cause cancer.

The same sections: reproductive toxicity, category 1B; the solution may damage fertility or the unborn child. This is a more severe statement than the H361f of the pure substance's entry in the PubChem record.
The same sections: specific target organ toxicity after a single exposure, category 2; the solution may damage organs.
Section 3.1: the weight percent of phenolphthalein. The same table gives water 55.59, ethanol 41.76, methanol 2.09 and sodium hydroxide below 0.1.
Section 2.2, prevention: keeping the solution away from heat, sparks, flames and other sources of ignition.
Section 2.2, prevention: protective gloves and eye protection.
